record.title: OpenAI's revised Raising Concerns Policy adds direct escalation of AI safety concerns to its Foundation board committee
record.summary: OpenAI's Oct 30 policy says personnel may escalate good-faith AI Safety Concerns directly to the OpenAI Foundation's Safety and Security Committee (SSC), or through the Integrity Line, where Compliance escalates them to the SSC. The policy states the SSC has full authority and any requested resources to address such concerns. It describes this pathway as a channel for input and consideration, not a formal investigation. The published policy establishes a stated process; it does not show that reports were made, that the route has been used, or that decisions or safety outcomes changed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI's Raising Concerns Policy PDF dated Oct 30 says personnel may raise good-faith AI Safety Concerns directly to the OpenAI Foundation's Safety and Security Committee (SSC), or through the Integrity Line; it says Compliance will escalate AI-safety reports made through that line to the SSC.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The policy says the SSC has full authority and any requested resources to address an AI Safety Concern, and clarifies that this pathway is not a formal investigation but a channel for safety input and consideration.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The published policy does not establish whether personnel have used the direct route, how concerns were resolved, or whether it changed decisions or safety outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: No evidence about real use, case handling or safety outcomes of the newly stated escalation route was found in the policy document.

brief.importance_rationale: If used as written, direct access to the OpenAI Foundation board's Safety and Security Committee with stated authority and requested resources could change escalation options for internal AI-safety concerns. The policy establishes a published process, not evidence that reports were made, resolved, or changed decisions.
limitations: This is an OpenAI-authored policy statement; it documents the stated process, not observed implementation.
The policy describes AI safety escalation as a channel for input and consideration rather than a formal investigation; do not imply every concern triggers a formal investigation.
No evidence was found about report counts, case decisions or resulting changes to safety practices.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI says the SSC will have full authority and any requested resources to address AI Safety Concerns raised through the stated process.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Oct 30 policy document contains a direct-to-SSC route and describes Compliance escalation for AI safety reports submitted through the Integrity Line.
technical.implementation_status: Published policy document; no independent evidence of implementation or operational use was reviewed.
technical.mechanism: Personnel may raise concerns through regular business channels, the 24/7 Integrity Line, or directly to the SSC. For AI safety concerns submitted through the Integrity Line, Compliance says it will escalate the concern to the SSC.
technical.regime: OpenAI Personnel under the Oct 30, 2026 Raising Concerns Policy; the process covers good-faith concerns about potential harm from OpenAI AI technology, products, models or services.
technical.strongest_baseline: The Jan 12 policy page says the prior policy provided multiple internal channels and that certain issues might be shared with the Audit Committee. The Oct 30 policy PDF now expressly describes direct SSC escalation for AI Safety Concerns; no comparison of every policy clause or prior implementation was performed.

brief.title: OpenAI's revised Raising Concerns Policy adds direct escalation of AI safety concerns to its Foundation board committee
brief.why_it_matters: A direct board-committee escalation route could change the formal options available to personnel raising internal AI safety concerns. The public policy is evidence of the stated process, not its use or effectiveness.
